question: Should routine restart-required `config.patch` and `config.apply` writes in hot mode keep the current direct-restart behavior, or may they warn-and-keep after the in-process write path refreshes runtime config?
rationale: This is a compatibility and runtime-coherence contract for gateway config writes; the code-only patch cannot safely choose a new RPC behavior without owner intent.

options.title: Preserve RPC Direct Restart
options.body: Keep current direct-restart behavior for routine restart-required hot-mode RPC writes while retaining the security-critical watcher/RPC carve-out.

options.title: Accept New RPC Contract With Snapshot Guard
options.body: Allow routine hot-mode RPC writes to warn-and-keep only if the implementation also proves restart-required settings do not become active in the runtime snapshot before restart.

options.title: Pause Behavior Change
options.body: Pause this PR and land diagnostics first if maintainers want more evidence before changing the hot-mode restart contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve RPC Direct Restart
recommendation.body: Keep current direct-restart behavior for routine restart-required hot-mode RPC writes while retaining the security-critical watcher/RPC carve-out.
